results.title: Asscher maakt excuses voor rol toeslagenaffaire  pijnlijke constateringen
results.src_text:
PvdA-leider Lodewijk Asscher heeft excuses aangeboden voor zijn rol in de kinderopvangtoeslagenaffaire. In reactie op een snoeihard rapport over de kwestie schrijft hij op Facebook: "De constateringen over mijn eigen rol hierin zijn pijnlijk en vervullen me met schaamte".
Asscher was van 2012 tot 2017 minister van Sociale Zaken. In die periode werden duizenden ouders door de Belastingdienst onterecht aangemerkt als fraudeur, met als gevolg dat ze soms tienduizenden euro's aan toeslagen moesten terugbetalen. Asscher was als minister niet verantwoordelijk voor de fiscus, maar wel voor de Wet kinderopvang waarin de kostenverdeling voor opvang is geregeld.
Vorige week oordeelde een parlementaire ondervragingscommissie dat ouders "ongekend onrecht" was aangedaan en dat beginselen van de rechtsstaat zijn geschonden. Asscher getuigde voor die commissie.
Het kabinet heeft in 2019 al excuses aangeboden. "Formeel is dat mede namens eerdere kabinetten en dus ook namens mij", schrijft Asscher. "Maar ik wil ook persoonlijk mijn excuses aanbieden aan iedereen die hierdoor geraakt is."
'Heb ik niet goed genoeg gedaan'
De oud-minister zegt dat er meerdere momenten waren waarop hij had kunnen doorvragen "om beter te begrijpen hoe hardvochtig de wetgeving op dit punt uitpakte voor sommige mensen". "Dat heb ik niet goed genoeg gedaan."
Asscher zegt verder dat er lessen getrokken moeten worden uit de affaire en dat gedupeerde ouders zo snel mogelijk gecompenseerd moeten worden.
results.tgt_text: PvdA leader Lodewijk Asscher has apologized for his role in the childcare allowance scandal. In response to a scathing report on the issue, he writes on Facebook: "The findings about my own role in this are painful and fill me with shame". Asscher was Minister of Social Affairs from 2012 to 2017. During that period, thousands of parents were wrongly classified as fraudsters by the tax authorities, with the result that they sometimes had to repay tens of thousands of euros in allowances. Asscher was not responsible for the tax authorities as Minister, but for the Childcare Act, which regulates the cost distribution for care.

Asscher was als minister niet verantwoordelijk voor de belastingdienst, maar voor de Wet kinderopvang, die de kostenverdeling voor opvang regelt.

results.title: Als het oplossen van opgaven faalt
results.src_text:
Het oplossen van (Natuurkunde) opgaven vraagt een heldere redeneerstijl en vaak ook enige structuur in de zoektocht naar het antwoord. Maar wat is er nu echt aan de hand als het niet lukt om een opgave goed uit te werken? In dit bericht kijk ik naar hoe een leerling geholpen kan worden.

In het boekje “Als de oplossing niet voor de hand ligt” wordt een werkwijze voorgesteld om opgaven systematisch aan te pakken: de Systematische Probleem Aanpak (SPA). We vragen leerlingen om de theorie goed door te nemen, veel te oefenen (alle opgaven te maken) en daarbij gebruik te maken van de Systematische Probleem Aanpak. Voor de meeste leerlingen is dit een effectieve strategie die daadwerkelijk goede resultaten oplevert.

Soms echter doet een leerling alles wat je voorstelt: de leerling let goed op in de les, maakt alle opgaven, werkt netjes en overzichtelijk, … maar scoort toch onder de maat. De frustratie wordt steeds groter en de motivatie van de leerling komt klem te zitten.

results.title: Harlingen (stad)
results.src_text:
Harlingen (Westerlauwers Fries: Harns ( uitspraak (info / uitleg))) is een stad in de Nederlandse provincie Friesland en de hoofdplaats van de gelijknamige gemeente.
Het ligt ten westen van Franeker en ten noorden van de Afsluitdijk aan de Waddenzee. Harlingen behoort tot de Friese elf steden. In 2020 telde de stad 14.740 inwoners. Het is de op vier na grootste plaats van Friesland. Tot de stad behoren ook de buurtschappen IJslumburen, Koetille, Koningsbuurt, Luidum en Ungabuurt. De haven van Harlingen is de belangrijkste haven van de provincie.

Ontstaan en stadsrechten
Omstreeks 1157 stichtte Eilwardus Ludinga het klooster Ludingakerke in het dorp Almenum. De monniken groeven grachten om de handelsvaart beter mogelijk te maken. Ludingakerk werd hierdoor een van de rijkste kloosters in Friesland. De buurt ten westen van Almenum, Harlingen, werd daardoor zó belangrijk dat deze in 1234 stadsrechten kreeg. Daarmee is Harlingen als stad ouder dan bijvoorbeeld Leeuwarden, Dokkum, Franeker of Amsterdam.

results.title: Spelregels motorrijder
results.src_text:
Ook motorrijders moeten zich aan een aantal spelregels houden als ze een file auto’s inhalen. In het algemeen moet er rekening mee worden gehouden dat motorrijders relatief slecht zichtbaar zijn voor automobilisten en dat automobilisten de snelheid van de motor slecht inschatten.

1. Gepaste snelheid
Rijd rustig tussen de file door. Dat wil zeggen dat het snelheidsverschil tussen de motor en de auto die u passeert, niet meer mag zijn dan 10 km/u. Houd deze vuistregel aan bij iedere auto die u passeert. Hoge snelheidsverschillen zijn de belangrijkste bron van irritatie bij automobilisten en zorgen voor gevaarlijke schrikreacties.

2. Wees alert op onvoorzichtig gedrag
Twee belangrijke manoeuvres waarvan motorrijders hinder ondervinden, zijn:
* bij gaten in de file: automobilisten die opeens van rijstrook wisselen
* bij warm weer: openstaande portieren van auto’s.

3. Meerdere motorrijders
Als met meerdere motoren wordt gereden, houd dan ook het hoofd koel en rij rustig achter elkaar tussen de file door. Houd onderling minstens een afstand van twee auto’s aan. Kies voor dezelfde doorgang.

4. Naderen file
Bij het naderen van een file houdt u via de spiegels rekening met achterop komend verkeer dat niet tijdig snelheid vermindert. Verminder zelf geleidelijk aan de snelheid en waarschuw achterop komend verkeer met alarmlichten (of remlicht). Om verwarring bij automobilisten te voorkomen
results.tgt_text: Motorcyclists must also adhere to a number of rules when overtaking a line of cars. In general, motorcyclists are relatively poorly visible to car drivers and car drivers have difficulty in judging the speed of a motorcycle. 1. Appropriate speed. Drive slowly between the traffic jam. This means that the speed difference between the motorcycle and the car you are passing must not be more than 10 km/h. Observe this rule for every car you pass. High speed differences are the main source of irritation for car drivers and cause dangerous panic reactions. 2. Be alert to careless behaviour. Two important manoeuvres that motorcyclists are inconvenienced by are: * when gaps appear in the traffic jam: car drivers who suddenly change lane. * in hot weather: open car doors. 3. Multiple motorcyclists. If multiple motorcycles are being driven, keep your head cool and drive calmly behind each other between the traffic jam. Keep a distance of at least two cars between each other. Choose the same route. 4. Approaching traffic jam. When approaching a traffic jam, keep an eye on traffic behind you that does not reduce speed in time. Gradually reduce your own speed and warn traffic behind you with alarm lights (or brake lights). To avoid confusion among car drivers
results.back_text: Motorrijders moeten zich ook aan een aantal regels houden bij het inhalen van een rij auto's. In het algemeen zijn motorrijders relatief slecht zichtbaar voor automobilisten en hebben automobilisten moeite met het inschatten van de snelheid van een motor. 1. Passende snelheid. Rijd langzaam tussen het verkeersopstopping. Dit betekent dat het snelheidsverschil tussen de motor en de auto die je passeert niet meer dan 10 km/u mag zijn. Houd deze regel aan voor elke auto die je passeert. Hoge snelheidsverschillen zijn de belangrijkste bron van irritatie voor automobilisten en veroorzaken gevaarlijke paniekaanvallen. 2. Wees alert op onvoorzichtig gedrag. Twee belangrijke manoeuvres waar motorrijders hinder van ondervinden zijn: * wanneer gaten in het verkeersopstopping verschijnen: automobilisten die plotseling van rijbaan wisselen. * in hete weersomstandigheden: open autodeuren. 3. Meerdere motorrijders. Als meerdere motoren worden bestuurd, blijf kalm en rij rustig achter elkaar tussen het verkeersopstopping. Houd minimaal twee auto's afstand tussen elkaar. Kies dezelfde route. 4. Naderend verkeersopstopping. Wanneer je een verkeersopstopping nadert, houd je de verkeer achter je in de gaten dat niet op tijd zijn snelheid verlaagt. Verminder geleidelijk je eigen snelheid en waarschuw het verkeer achter je met alarmlichten (of remlichten). Om verwarring bij automobilisten te voorkomen

'I don't want to go in the water now,' Janelle said. 'Let's go and have a drink at the caf,.' Brian sat on his surfboard and watched Nick in the water. 'Mike and Janelle are wrong,' he thought. results.src_text:
Living in the valley

We had been living in our valley for sixteen months when we first realised the dangers that could exist in the surrounding hills and threaten our very survival.
It was the year when the storms came early, before the calendar even hinted at winter, even before November was out. Until that time, we had felt safe and sheltered in our valley below the protecting hills.
Soon snow began to fall. Within a day it lay some 15 centimetres deep. It almost completely blocked our lane and made the streamside path slippery and dangerous. But on the neighbouring heights the snow was much deeper and stayed for longer. Up there the wind blasted fiercely. Deep in our valley we felt only sudden gusts of wind; trees swayed but the branches held firm.
And yet we knew that there was reason for us to worry. The snow and wind were certainly inconvenient but they did not really trouble us greatly. It was the river, the Ryburn, which normally flowed so gently, that threatened us most. It reminded us of what could have occurred if circumstances had been different, if the flow of water from the hills had not, many years before, been controlled, held back by a series of dams.
In a short time the snow started to melt. Day after day, we watched furious clouds pile up high over the hills to the west. Sinister grey clouds extended over the valleys. They twisted and turned, rising eastwards and upwards, warning of what was to come. We had seen enough of the sky; now we began to watch the river, which every day was becoming fuller and wilder.
The snow was gradually washed away as more and more rain streamed from the clouds, but high up in the hills the reservoir was filling and was fast approaching danger level. And then it happened - for the first time in years the reservoir overflowed. There in the heights it was like the Niagara Falls, as the water surged over the edge of the dam and poured into the stream below. 
The river seemed maddened as the waters poured almost horizontally down to its lower stretches. Just a couple of metres from our cottage, the stream seemed wild beneath the bridge. It was far deeper than we'd ever seen it so near our home, lunging furiously at its banks. For three days we prayed that it would stay below its wall. Fortunately, our prayers were answered as the dam held and the waters began to subside.
On many occasions through the centuries before the dam was built, the river had flooded the nearby villages in just such a rage. Now, though, the dam restricts the flow of the river and usually all is well; the great mass of water from the hills, the product of snow and torrential rain, remains behind its barrier with just the occasional overflow. We can thus enjoy, rather than fear, the huge clouds that hang over the valley, and can be thrilled by the tremendous power which we know the river possesses. Thanks to this protection we can feel our home in the valley is still secure and safe.

Tot die tijd hadden we ons veilig en beschut gevoeld in ons dal onder de beschermende heuvels. Al snel viel er sneeuw. Binnen een dag lag deze 15 centimeter diep. De doorgang naar ons huis was bijna volledig geblokkeerd en de oever van de beek was glad en gevaarlijk. Maar op de omliggende heuvels lag de sneeuw veel dieper en bleef langer liggen. Daar waailde de wind hevig. In ons dal voelden we alleen plotselinge windvlagen. Bomen zwaaiden maar de takken bleven stevig aan de boom. En toch wisten we dat we ons zorgen moesten maken. De sneeuw en wind waren zeker hinderlijk maar ze brachten ons niet in grote problemen. Het was de rivier, de Ryburn, die normaal zo rustig stroomde, die ons het meest bedreigde. Ze herinnerde ons aan wat er had kunnen gebeuren als de omstandigheden anders waren geweest, als de stroom van water van de heuvels niet vele jaren eerder was beheerst, tegengehouden door een reeks dammen. In korte tijd begon de sneeuw te smelten. Dag na dag keken we naar de woeste wolken die zich hoog boven de heuvels in het westen stapelden. Smerige grijze wolken strekten zich uit over de valleien. Ze draaiden en kronkelden, opstijgend naar het oosten en naar boven, waarschuwend voor wat er zou komen. We hadden genoeg gezien van de lucht; nu begonnen we de rivier te bekijken, die elke dag voller en wilder werd. De sneeuw werd geleidelijk weggespoeld door meer en meer regen die uit de wolken stroomde, maar hoog op de heuvels vulde het stuwmeer zich snel en naderde het gevaarlijk niveau. We kunnen dus genieten, in plaats van bang te zijn, van de enorme wolken die boven het dal hangen, en kunnen worden geënthousiasmeerd door de enorme kracht die we weten dat de rivier bezit. Dankzij deze bescherming kunnen we ons huis in het dal nog steeds veilig en veilig voelen.

results.tgt_text: Nous avons vécu dans notre vallée pendant seize mois lorsque nous avons réalisé pour la première fois les dangers qui pouvaient exister dans les collines environnantes et menacer notre survie. Ce fut l'année où les tempêtes sont arrivées tôt, avant même que le calendrier ne laisse entrevoir l'hiver, même avant que novembre ne soit terminé. Jusqu'à ce moment, nous nous sentions en sécurité et abrités dans notre vallée en dessous des collines protectrices. Bientôt, la neige a commencé à tomber. En l'espace d'un jour, elle était tombée à environ 15 centimètres de profondeur. Elle a presque complètement bloqué notre allée et rendu le chemin près de la rivière glissant et dangereux. Mais sur les hauteurs voisines, la neige était beaucoup plus profonde et restait plus longtemps. Là-haut, le vent soufflait avec violence. Dans notre vallée, nous avons senti seulement de soudains coups de vent ; les arbres s'agitaient, mais les branches tenaient fermes. Et pourtant, nous savions que nous avions raison de nous inquiéter. La neige et le vent étaient certes gênants, mais ils ne nous ont pas vraiment troublés. C'était la rivière, le Ryburn, qui normalement coulait si doucement, qui nous menaçait le plus. Elle nous a rappelé ce qui aurait pu se produire si les circonstances avaient été différentes, si le débit d'eau des collines n'avait pas été, de nombreuses années auparavant, contrôlé, retenu par une série de barrages. En peu de temps, la neige a commencé à fondre. Jour après jour, nous avons regardé des nuages furieux s'amonceler haut dans les collines à l'ouest. Des nuages gris sinistres s'étendaient sur les vallées. Ils se sont retournés, se levant vers l'est et vers le haut, avertissant de ce qui devait arriver. Nous avons vu assez du ciel ; maintenant, nous avons commencé à regarder la rivière, qui chaque jour devenait plus pleine et plus sauvage. La neige a été progressivement lavée par une pluie plus abondante, mais en haut des collines, le réservoir se remplissait et approchait rapidement du niveau dangereux. Et puis cela est arrivé - pour la première fois en années, le réservoir a débordé. Là, dans les hauteurs, c'était comme le Niagara Falls, alors que l'eau dévalait le rebord du barrage et se déversait dans le ruisseau en contrebas. La rivière semblait folle alors que les eaux déferlaient presque horizontalement vers ses parties inférieures. À seulement deux mètres de notre maison, le ruisseau semblait sauvage sous le pont. Il était bien plus profond qu'on ne l'avait jamais vu si près de notre maison, se déchaînant furieusement contre ses rives. Pendant trois jours, nous avons prié pour qu'il reste en dessous de sa paroi. Heureusement, nos prières ont été exaucées car le barrage a tenu et les eaux ont commencé à baisser. À de nombreuses reprises au cours des siècles avant la construction du barrage, la rivière avait inondé les villages voisins dans une telle rage. Maintenant, cependant, le barrage restreint le débit de la rivière et, en général, tout va bien ; la grande masse d'eau des collines, le produit de la neige et des pluies torrentielles, reste derrière sa barrière avec juste le débordement occasionnel. Nous pouvons ainsi apprécier, plutôt que craindre, les énormes nuages qui se dressent dans la vallée, et nous pouvons être émerveillés par la puissance énorme que nous savons posséder la rivière. Grâce à cette protection, nous pouvons sentir que notre maison dans la vallée est toujours sûre et sécurisée.

results.src_text:
We are being bombarded with advertisements all the time and a lot of them are targeted at young people. Smaller children, apart from spending their own pocket money, can also influence what their parents buy, so many TV ads are created with kids in mind. 
For example, adverts for drinks feature cartoon animals. Then, as two-year-olds are being pushed around the shop by their parents in a trolley, they recognise the drink from the advert and ask the adults to buy it. As children grow older, some products are marketed to them as 'must-have' items, implying that children won't be liked by their friends if they don't get them. 
As a result, kids are desperate to get the product and parents can be made to feel guilty if they don't buy it for their child. Teenagers are incredibly critical of adverts, so products aimed at them have to be advertised much more cleverly. As teens are driven by the desire to be part of the 'coolest' group in their school, products need to be given a cool feel. 
For example, advertisers give away stickers which direct teens to a difficult-to-find website with more information about a product. In this way, naturally rebellious teens feel that they have been invited to an exclusive club and can be sold expensive products. 
As teens hate being influenced by adults, marketers let them persuade each other that a certain product is cool. Since the late nineties, 'street teams' of teenagers have been employed by clothing and record companies to spread the word about a product among young people.

Les enfants sont alors désireux d'obtenir le produit et les parents peuvent être amenés à se sentir coupables s'ils ne l'achètent pas pour leur enfant. Les adolescents sont extrêmement critiques envers les publicités, de sorte que les produits destinés à eux doivent être commercialisés de manière beaucoup plus intelligente. Comme les adolescents sont poussés par le désir d'être membres du groupe le plus cool de leur école, les produits doivent avoir une image cool. Par exemple, les annonceurs distribuent des autocollants qui dirigent les adolescents vers un site Web difficile à trouver avec plus d'informations sur un produit. De cette façon, les adolescents naturellement rebelles se sentent invités à rejoindre un club exclusif et peuvent se faire vendre des produits chers. Comme les adolescents détestent être influencés par les adultes, les marketeurs les laissent persuader les uns les autres qu'un produit est cool. Depuis la fin des années 1990, des « street teams » de jeunes sont employés par des sociétés de vêtements et de disques pour faire la promotion d'un produit auprès des jeunes.
results.back_text: We are bombarded with advertising all the time and many of them are aimed at young people. Younger people, in addition to spending their own pocket money, can also influence their parents' purchases. Many television adverts are therefore created with children in mind. For example, drinks adverts feature cartoon animals. As parents push their two-year-old child in a pushchair around the shop, the child recognises the drink from the advert and asks their parents to buy it. As children grow older, many products are marketed to them, making them believe that they will not be popular with their friends if they do not own them. Children then want to get the product and parents may feel guilty if they do not buy it for their child. Teenagers are extremely critical of advertising, so products aimed at them must be marketed much more cleverly. As teenagers are driven by a desire to be part of the coolest group at their school, products must have a cool image. For example, advertisers distribute stickers that direct teenagers to a hard-to-find website with more information about a product. In this way, naturally rebellious teenagers feel invited to join an exclusive club and can be sold expensive products. As teenagers hate being influenced by adults, marketeers let them persuade each other that a product is cool. Since the late 1990s,'street teams' of young people have been employed by clothing and record companies to promote a product to young people.

Lexington, who had always done everything his aunt had told him, put the money in his pocket, put on a pair of shoes and a clean shirt, and went down the mountain to the village where the doctor lived.
'Old Glosspan?' the doctor said. 'Is she dead?'
'Certainly she's dead,' the boy answered. 'If you come home with me now I'll dig her up and you can see for yourself.'
'How deep did you bury her?' the doctor asked. 'Two or three metres down, I think.' 
'And how long ago?' 'Oh, about eight hours.' 'Then she's dead,' the doctor announced. 'Here's the certificate.'
Lexington now left for the city of New York to find Mr Samuel Zuckermann. He travelled on foot, and he slept under bushes, and he lived on berries and wild plants, and it took him sixteen days to reach the city.
'What a place this is!' he cried, as he stood staring around him. 'There are no chickens or cows anywhere and none of the women looks like Aunt Glosspan at all.'
Lexington had never seen anyone like Mr Zuckermann before, either. He was a small man with a large nose, and when he smiled, bits of gold flashed at you from lots of different places inside his
mouth. In his office, he shook Lexington warmly by the hand and congratulated him on his aunt's death.
'I suppose you know that your dearly loved aunt was a woman of great wealth?' he said.
'Do you mean the cows and the chickens?'
'I mean five hundred thousand dollars,' Mr Zuckermann said.
'How much?'
'Five hundred thousand dollars, my boy. And she's left it all to you.'

"There's something out there! It threw an orange at me!" Elliott said. "Ooooo!" said Tyler, a friend of Elliott. "An orange! Very dangerous!" Elliott's mom, Mary, took a light, and then she and the boys went into the yard. "What did you see?" Mary asked Elliott. "Something there," he answered. He pointed to the end of the yard. Elliott's brother, Michael, said, "Look, something walked across the ground here!" The extra-terrestrial looked at them from the dark. There were five Earth children, and a tall, beautiful person. Strange sounds came from her mouth. He couldn't understand them. Was she their mother? His heart-light started to shine, so he put his hand over it. She was the most beautiful of Earth people. 
The extra-terrestrial looked and looked. "Stupid heart-light," he said-but it shone more and more. The Earth people went back into the kitchen. Later in the night, three of the children left the house. They were Elliott's friends, Greg, Tyler, and Steve. Then, the lights went out and the house was quiet. The extra-terrestrial walked across the yard to the plants. It was very dark now, so he couldn't see. He hit his head and fell back on the ground.
He cried out loudly. Suddenly, the kitchen door opened and Elliott ran out into the yard with his dog, Harvey. He shone a light into the plants and saw the extraterrestrial. Elliott shouted-and fell over. The extra-terrestrial started to run.
"Don't go!" Elliott said.

Elliott's moeder, Mary, pakte een zaklamp en toen gingen ze met de jongens naar de achtertuin. "Wat heb je gezien?" vroeg Mary Elliott. "Iets daar," antwoordde hij. Hij wees naar het einde van de tuin. Elliotts broer, Michael, zei: "Kijk, iets is hier over de grond gelopen!" De buitenaardse wezen keek vanuit de duisternis naar hen. Zijn hartlicht begon te stralen, dus hij legde zijn hand erover. Ze was de mooiste van alle aardse mensen.

Growing up in Los Angeles, Vanessa Van Petten got into trouble so often that her mother and father began buying parenting advice books. 
During one of her frequent groundings, Van Petten glanced through several of the books and spotted what she considered two major problems. 
First, the books provided useless advice. More importantly, they were written by adults with no input from teenagers. That's when Van Petten decided to take matters into her own hands. 
At the age of sixteen, she wrote a book for parents from the teenage perspective: You're Grounded: How to Stop Fighting and Make the Teenage Years Easier. 
By the age of twenty-one, she had created RadicalParenting.com, an online community for parents and teens. That's where, with two full-time employees, Van Petten's 120 bloggers aged twelve to twenty answer questions from parents. The site generates revenue through advertising and sponsored links to other websites. 
Vanessa's advice: 
Get advice and help: 'Everyone said I was too young to start a company but I used online resources, read books, attended conferences and got advice from people I know. That's how I learnt about the business so quickly.' 
Reach new audiences: 'Social media is a great way to get in touch with new users - that's why we went on sites for mums and personally emailed videos to big users in each community.' 
Do something that works: 'Most importantly, we offered advice that actually works. Parents increasingly began spreading our quirky and sometimes controversial articles by word of mouth. We want to build a brand that is not only interesting but also life-changing.'

This is a lovely novel that all age groups can understand. Aimed at native English speaking children, there are many adults who still say this famous book is their favorite. This is part of the national curriculum in many schools around the world, so it’s quite possible this book will also come up in conversation. You can almost guarantee that the majority of native English speakers have read this book at least once.
Plot Summary
A baby pig is almost killed because of his status – he is the smallest pig that was born and he is considered to be useless and of no value. The pig is saved by a little girl called Fern Arable. She adopts the pig and takes care of it. She gives him the name Wilbur.
Fern grows sad when Wilbur grows up and has to be sent away to a farm owned by her uncle. She has a strong relationship with Wilbur. When Wilbur goes to the farm, all the other farm animals ignore him and he’s left crying for his human friend. One day he hears a voice, but he can’t see anything. This voice promises to become friends with him.
The voice belongs to a small spider called Charlotte. Charlotte the spider knows that the farmers are planning to kill Wilbur. She promises to make a plan to save his life. The farmers are surprised the next day when they see the words “some pig” written in the web* Charlotte has made. Charlotte asked for the other animals’ help over the day to write messages everywhere.
Wilbur is sad when Charlotte disappears. But in the end, her baby spiders turn out to be great company for the pig. They continue to protect each other and the story ends well.

Dit is onderdeel van het nationale curriculum op veel scholen over de hele wereld, dus het is vrijwel zeker dat dit boek ook in gesprek komt. Je kunt bijna garanderen dat de meerderheid van de Engelssprekende mensen dit boek al minstens een keer heeft gelezen.

A baby pig is almost killed because of his status – he is the smallest pig that was born and he is considered to be useless and of no value. The pig is saved by a little girl called Fern Arable. She adopts the pig and takes care of it. She gives him the name Wilbur.
Fern grows sad when Wilbur grows up and has to be sent away to a farm owned by her uncle. She has a strong relationship with Wilbur. When Wilbur goes to the farm, all the other farm animals ignore him and he’s left crying for his human friend. One day he hears a voice, but he can’t see anything. This voice promises to become friends with him.
The voice belongs to a small spider called Charlotte. Charlotte the spider knows that the farmers are planning to kill Wilbur. She promises to make a plan to save his life. The farmers are surprised the next day when they see the words “some pig” written in the web* Charlotte has made. Charlotte asked for the other animals’ help over the day to write messages everywhere.
Wilbur is sad when Charlotte disappears. But in the end, her baby spiders turn out to be great company for the pig. They continue to protect each other and the story ends well.

THEATRE

CHARLES SPENCER

A. Tamburlaine the Great

Marlowe’s ten-act epic about the all-conquering warrior can seem never-ending, but it emerges as one of the most thrilling nights of the year in Terry Hands’ staging. He has hacked great chunks from the text and offers a production that combines the glories of Marlowe’s play with an exhilarating speed and physicality. Antony Sher is in terrific form in the title role, somersaulting from the balcony, sliding down a rope head-first as he delivers a speech, demanding and getting the audience’s complete attention as his eyes glint with a mad lust for power and glory. Great stuff.
Swan Theatre, Stratford-upon-Avon (01789 295623)

B. Women Laughing

Welcome London transfer for the late Michael Wall’s fine play, seen at the Manchester Royal Exchange in May. The first act creates an atmosphere of unsettling menace as two married couples chat on a sunny suburban lawn. In the second half the location shifts and the piece becomes a powerful, compassionate study of the devastating effects of illness. The British theatre lost a talent of great promise when Wall died at the tragically early age of 44.
Royal Court Theatre, London SW1 (0207 730 1745)

C. Amphibians

Billy Roche is the latest in the long line of Irish dramatists to have enriched the English stage. All his plays to date have been set in his native Wexford, and this latest piece explores the decline of the fishing industry with his usual mixture of rich characterisation, painful emotion and sudden moments of quirky humour. The play sprawls a bit aimlessly at times, but builds to a blistering climax.
Barbican 3 Pit Theatre, London EC2 (0207 638 8891)

D. Murder by Misadventure

Traditional thriller involving our old friend, ‘the perfect murder’. This time it is Gerald Harper and William Gaunt who play the crime-writing partnership intent on killing each other, and though its all rather familiar stuff; the twists and turns are handled with ingenuity.
Whitehall Theatre, London SW1 (0207 867 1119)

E. The Alchemist

Young director Sam Mendes finds the gold in Jonson’s great comedy of 17th-century confidence tricksters. First seen at the Swan in Stratford last year, the show works just as well on the Barbican’s main stage, with Jonathan Hyde, David Bradley and Joanne Pearce repeating their fine performances as the wicked trio of con-artists.
Barbican Theatre, London EC2 (0207 638 8891)

F. The Madras House

Peter James’ production of Harley Granville Barkers rich, panoramic comedy about fashion and the position of women in Edwardian society transfers to London after its success at the Edinburgh Festival. The staging is stylish, the acting excellent, the play itself an unjustly neglected classic.
Lyric Theatre, Hammersmith, London W6 (0208 741 2311)

G. Dreams from a summer house

This delightful new musical finds playwright Alan Ayckbourn in unusually benign form as he relocates the Beauty and the Beast story deep in the heart of London suburbia. A lush score by John Pattison and an unashamedly schmaltzy celebration of romantic love combine to make this good-hearted show a real winner. London impresarios looking for a hit should board the next train to Scarborough.
Stephen Joseph Theatre, Scarborough (01 723 370541)

H. The Merry Wives of Windsor

David Thacker’s lacklustre production of Shakespeare’s most farcical comedy came perilously close to being awarded the dreaded thumbs-down symbol, but this disappointing, crudely designed show is redeemed by first-rate comic performances from Ron Cook as the French physician Dr Caius and Anton Lesser as the explosively jealous husband, Ford. Almost everyone else looks faintly embarrassed, as well they might.
Shakespeare Theatre, Stragford-upon-Avon (01789 295623)

I. The Voysey Inheritance

Another major Granville Barker revival, now touring the regions. This story of an apparently respectable solicitor who bequeaths a corrupt financial legacy to his son results in a marvellous play.
Apollo Theatre, Oxford (01865 244544)

A. Tamburlaine the Great

Marlowe’s tiendelige epische over de allesoverwinnende krijger kan eindeloos lijken, maar het wordt een van de meest opwindende avonden van het jaar in Terry Hands’ regie. Hij heeft grote stukken uit het stuk gehakt en biedt een productie die de glorie van Marlowe’s toneelstuk combineert met een opwindende snelheid en fysieke kracht. Antony Sher is in een fantastische vorm in de titelrol, hij klimt vanaf het balkon en glijdt hoofd-de-jato naar beneden terwijl hij een toespraak houdt, en eist de volledige aandacht van het publiek op, terwijl zijn ogen glanzen met een waanzinnige lust naar macht en glorie. Geweldig.
Swan Theatre, Stratford-upon-Avon (01789 295623)

B. Women Laughing

Welkom in Londen voor de mooie productie van Michael Wall’s mooie toneelstuk, dat in mei te zien was in Manchester. In de eerste act creëert de stuk een sfeer van onheilspellend gevaar terwijl twee echtparen op een zonnig buitengewoon praten. In de tweede helft verandert de locatie en wordt het stuk een krachtige, mededogenvolle studie van de verwoestende effecten van ziekte. Het Britse theater heeft een talent van grote belofte verloren toen Wall op tragisch jonge leeftijd van 44 overleed.
Royal Court Theatre, London SW1 (0207 730 1745)

C. Amphibians

Billy Roche is de nieuwste in de lange rij van Ierse toneelschrijvers die het Engelse toneel hebben verrijkt. Al zijn stukken tot nu toe zijn in zijn geboortestad Wexford gesitueerd en dit laatste stuk verkent de neergang van de visserijindustrie met zijn gebruikelijke mix van rijke personageschetsen, pijnlijke emoties en plotselinge momenten van eigenaardige humor. Het stuk is soms wat wazig, maar bereikt een branderig hoogtepunt.
Barbican 3 Pit Theatre, London EC2 (0207 638 8891)

D. Murder by Misadventure

Traditionele thriller met onze oude vriend, ‘de perfecte moord’. Deze keer spelen Gerald Harper en William Gaunt de misdaadschrijvende partners die elkaar willen vermoorden, en hoewel het allemaal best vertrouwd is, worden de wendingen met vernuft aangepakt.
Whitehall Theatre, London SW1 (0207 867 1119)

E. The Alchemist

De jonge regisseur Sam Mendes vindt goud in Jonson’s grote komedie over de vertrouwensrelatie in de 17e eeuw. Voor het eerst te zien in het Swan in Stratford vorig jaar, is de show net zo goed te zien op de grote scène van het Barbican, met Jonathan Hyde, David Bradley en Joanne Pearce die hun fantastische prestaties herhalen als de drie boze oplichters.
Barbican Theatre, London EC2 (0207 638 8891)

F. The Madras House

Peter James’ productie van Harley Granville Barkers rijke, panoramische komedie over mode en de positie van vrouwen in de Edwardiaanse samenleving wordt na een succesvolle tournee in Edinburgh naar Londen gebracht. De opstelling is stijlvol, de acteerprestaties uitstekend en de play zelf is een onverdiende klassieker.
Lyric Theatre, Hammersmith, London W6 (0208 741 2311)

G. Dreams from a summer house

Dit aangename nieuwe musical vindt de schrijver Alan Ayckbourn in ongewoon vriendelijke vorm als hij het sprookje van de Beer en de Bijen diep in het hart van het Londense voorstedenleven plaatst. Een weelderige score van John Pattison en een ongegeneerde romantische viering van de liefde maken van deze goedhartige show een echte winnaar. Londense impresario’s op zoek naar een hit moeten de volgende trein naar Scarborough nemen.
Stephen Joseph Theatre, Scarborough (01 723 370541)

H. The Merry Wives of Windsor

David Thacker’s matige productie van Shakespeare’s meest farceuze komedie kwam bedroevend dicht bij de verwerpelijke duim omhoog tekening, maar deze benauwende, slecht ontworpen show wordt vergeven door eersteklas komische prestaties van Ron Cook als de Franse arts Dr Caius en Anton Lesser als de explosief jaloerse echtgenoot, Ford. Vrijwel iedereen ziet er flauw uit, net zoals ze zouden moeten.
Shakespeare Theatre, Stragford-upon-Avon (01789 295623)

I. The Voysey Inheritance

Nog een belangrijke Granville Barker heruitgave, nu op tournee in de regio. Deze verhaal over een schijnbaar respectabele advocaat die een corrupt financieel erfenis nalaat aan zijn zoon resulteert in een prachtig stuk.
Apollo Theatre, Oxford (01865 244544)

results.tgt_text:
THEATRE

CHARLES SPENCER

A. Tamburlaine the Great

L’épopée de Tamburlaine, le conquérant, de Marlowe peut sembler interminable, mais elle se révèle être l’une des soirées les plus palpitantes de l’année dans la mise en scène de Terry Hands. Il a supprimé de grands morceaux du texte et propose une production qui allie les gloires de la pièce de Marlowe à une vitesse et une puissance physique exaltantes. Antony Sher est en pleine forme dans le rôle-titre, sautant du balcon, glissant par la corde la tête la première pendant qu’il prononce un discours, exigeant et obtenant l’attention complète du public tandis que ses yeux brillent d’une soif de pouvoir et de gloire. Superbe.
Swan Theatre, Stratford-upon-Avon (01789 295623)

B. Women Laughing

Transfert bienvenu à Londres pour la pièce fine de Michael Wall, vue au Manchester Royal Exchange en mai. Le premier acte crée une atmosphère d’insoutenable menace alors que deux couples mariés discutent sur un pré boisé ensoleillé. Dans la deuxième partie, le lieu change et la pièce devient une étude puissante et pleine de compassion des effets dévastateurs de la maladie. Le théâtre britannique a perdu un talent prometteur lorsque Wall est mort à l’âge tragique de 44 ans.
Royal Court Theatre, Londres SW1 (0207 730 1745)

C. Amphibians

Billy Roche est le dernier d’une longue lignée de dramaturges irlandais à avoir enrichi la scène anglaise. Tous ses pièces à ce jour ont été situées dans sa ville natale de Wexford, et cette dernière pièce explore le déclin de l’industrie de la pêche avec sa mixture habituelle de personnages richement caractérisés, d’émotions douloureuses et de moments d’humour bizarres. La pièce s’étire un peu sans direction, mais mène à une explosion finale.
Barbican 3 Pit Theatre, Londres EC2 (0207 638 8891)

D. Murder by Misadventure

Traditionnel thriller mettant en vedette notre vieil ami, le « meurtre parfaits ». Cette fois, c’est Gerald Harper et William Gaunt qui incarnent le partenariat de crime-writing déterminé à se tuer mutuellement, et bien que l’histoire soit assez familière, les rebondissements sont traités avec ingéniosité.
Whitehall Theatre, Londres SW1 (0207 867 1119)

E. The Alchemist

Le jeune metteur en scène Sam Mendes trouve l’or dans la grande comédie de Jonson sur les escrocs de la fin du XVIIe siècle. D’abord vue au Swan à Stratford l’année dernière, la pièce fonctionne tout aussi bien sur la scène principale du Barbican, avec Jonathan Hyde, David Bradley et Joanne Pearce qui répètent leurs excellentes performances en tant que trio de con-artistes méchants.
Barbican Theatre, Londres EC2 (0207 638 8891)

F. The Madras House

La production de Peter James de la riche comédie panoramique de Harley Granville Barker sur la mode et la position des femmes dans la société edwardienne est transférée à Londres après son succès au Festival d’Édimbourg. La mise en scène est élégante, les acteurs excellents, et l’œuvre elle-même est une oeuvre classique injustement négligée.
Lyric Theatre, Hammersmith, Londres W6 (0208 741 2311)

G. Dreams from a summer house

Ce charmant nouveau musical trouve le dramaturge Alan Ayckbourn dans une forme bienveillante inhabituelle alors qu’il relocalise l’histoire de la Belle et la Bête au cœur du quartier résidentiel londonien. Une partition luxuriante de John Pattison et une célébration naïve et mielleuse de l’amour amoureux se combinent pour faire de ce spectacle de bonne volonté un véritable succès. Les imprésarios londoniens à la recherche d’un succès devraient prendre le prochain train pour Scarborough.
Stephen Joseph Theatre, Scarborough (01 723 370541)

H. The Merry Wives of Windsor

La production décevante de David Thacker de la comédie la plus farfelue de Shakespeare se trouve à un moment où elle est en danger d’être désignée comme « mauvaise ». Cette production mal conçue et crudement dessinée est cependant réhabilitée par des performances comiques de premier ordre de Ron Cook en tant que médecin français Dr Caius et d’Anton Lesser en tant qu’époux jaloux et explosif, Ford. Presque tout le monde semble avoir l’air un peu gêné, comme ils le devraient.
Shakespeare Theatre, Stragford-upon-Avon (01789 295623)

I. The Voysey Inheritance

Une autre grande réédition de Granville Barker, en tournée actuellement. Cette histoire d’un avocat apparemment respectable qui légue un héritage corrompu à son fils se traduit en une merveilleuse pièce.
Apollo Theatre, Oxford (01865 244544)

results.src_text:
In September 1533 Anne gave birth to a daughter, Elizabeth (the future Queen Elizabeth I). Henry had grown tired of her, and after two further pregnancies ended in miscarriages, she was arrested in 1536 on trumped up charges of adultery and publicly beheaded at the Tower of London.
Henry's third marriage, this time to lady-in-waiting, Jane Seymour, finally produced the son he so desperately desired with the birth of Edward in 1537. Jane Seymour died after childbirth and Henry ordered that she be granted a queen's funeral.
In an attempt to establish ties with the German Protestant alliance, Thomas Cromwell arranged a marriage between the king and German princess Anne of Cleves. The marriage was a disaster and Henry divorced Anne a few months later. Henry blamed Cromwell for this mismatch and soon afterwards had him executed for treason.
The final years of his reign witnessed Henry VIII's physical decline and an increasing desire to appear all-powerful. Henry continued with fruitless and expensive campaigns against Scotland and France.
In 1540, the aging King married the teenage Catherine Howard. Their marriage was short lived. It was alleged that she had a previous relationship with Henry's courtier Francis Dereham and an affair with another courtier Thomas Culpeper. Catherine was executed for adultery and treason in 1542.
Henry's final marriage to Catherine Parr, who acted like a nurse, was more harmonious and she would go on to outlive him.
Henry VIII died on 28 January 1547 and was succeeded by his son, Edward VI. He was buried next to Jane Seymour in St. George's Chapel at Windsor Castle.

TIM RICE

I was ushered into the young man’s drawing room, an oasis of cultured sanity surrounded by what appeared to be a quite shambolic cluster of rooms in which the less enterprising members of the family operated. Moving from the kitchen to his parlour was an upgrade from economy to business class.
Here was the largest collection of records I had ever seen, the first stereo record player and tuner I had come across and the astonishing evidence that a teenager existed who had spent money on Georgian wine glasses, pictures and furniture.
His name was Andrew Lloyd Webber. He had won a scholarship to Magdalen College, Oxford, to read history, and he had nine months to kill before going up, during which time he intended to become England’s answer to the composer Richard Rodgers.
My own ambitions were just as insane as his, I wanted to be a pop star, for all the healthy reasons women, money and fame. The difference between Andrew and myself was that my dreams were never life or death to me, though it's easy to say that now. They might have become so had I failed.
Consequently, when Andrew suggested a completely new insane ambition for me, i.e. to become as famous a lyricist as Oscar Hammerstein, I had no qualms about giving it a go. This was partly because within ten minutes of our introduction, he was at the piano and had played me three tunes he had composed — I could tell that he was good. Very good.
As he confidently continued to bash out selections from some of the many shows he had written and produced at school, I was reminded of many of the best show albums from my parents LP collection. He needed a new lyricist for the outside world.
I had little to impress him with in return, other than instant praise for his music and a bona fide, actually released, seven-inch single of a song I had written (both words and music) with which an unknown pop group had dealt the final blow to their moribund career by recording three months previously. We parted, promising to meet again and to write something together. I was still more interested in the charts than in the West End theatre, but told myself on the bus back to my flat that I had just met somebody of rare ability and determination, and I would be mad to miss out on being a sidekick to a chap who was clearly going to take the musical theatre by storm, probably by next week.
And even if the two of us failed to challenge the top musical composers successfully, then we could try to knock the Beatles and Rolling Stones off their perches later, in the summer. The Everly Brothers had just made a comeback and would clearly be in need of some new material.
The next day, back at my desk in the office where I was training to become a solicitor, the brief certainty I had enjoyed of a life in show business with Andrew Lloyd Webber had faded somewhat. I would of course continue to keep an eye on the small ads in Melody Maker for groups needing a vocalist, and would turn out a few more three-chord songs tailored not to expose the limitations of my voice, but it was still odds-on that eventually I would stagger through my exams and wind up a respectable lawyer by the time I was twenty-five.
By then I would have surely grown out of pop music as my father had confidently predicted I would by the time I was twenty-one. This was worrying - if he was right I only had a few more months of enjoying it.
But in the meantime I felt I had nothing to lose by seeing Andrew again. It would be fun to go and see a musical with him, to write words that aped musical lyricists rather than pop stars. And Andrew was a fascinating individual who talked of Good Food Guides and Victorian architecture, besides supporting Leyton Orient football team.
I wasn’t convinced by the idea for a musical that he had been working on for the past year, but in 1965 I was rarely convinced about anything. His talent was beyond question and he claimed to have all the contacts. I was soon back in his drawing room.
The idea was the life of Dr Thomas Barnardo, the nineteenth century philanthropist who founded the orphanages that bear his name. His story was a worthy one indeed, but not one that truly fired my imagination. The hero was too squeaky-clean, at least in Andrew’s version of his life, and the enterprise was unoriginal in both conception and execution, owing far too much to Lionel Bart’s hit show, Oliver.
On the other hand, Andrew’s conviction of his score’s precocious brilliance was infectious and not totally unjustified. What did I know about musicals? As David Land, later to be my agent for over a quarter of a century, memorably (and repeatedly) said, if there’s a demand for one hamburger bar on the block, there is room for two. We could be the second hamburger joint.
I set to work with enormous enthusiasm, in particular for those songs that were intended to be funny. Andrew outlined the plot, played me the tunes and in many instances gave me the title as well, most of which had presumably been thought up by his ex-wordsmith school pal who had already had a go. I skipped a day at the solicitors office, faking illness, to write my first batch of theatrical lyrics. I did not know it that day but I had changed careers.

results.tgt_text: J'ai été invité dans le salon du jeune homme, une oasis de santé culturelle entourée de ce qui semblait être un groupe de pièces assez désordonnées dans lesquelles opéraient les membres les moins entreprenants de la famille. Passer de la cuisine à son salon était une mise à niveau de la classe économique à la classe affaires. Voici la plus grande collection de disques que j'ai jamais vue, le premier lecteur stéréo et l'enregistreur que j'ai rencontrés et l'étonnante preuve qu'un adolescent existait qui avait dépensé de l'argent pour des verres à vin géorgien, des photos et du mobilier. Son nom était Andrew Lloyd Webber. Il avait obtenu une bourse pour Magdalen College, Oxford, pour lire l'histoire et il avait neuf mois à tuer avant de monter, pendant lesquels il avait l'intention de devenir la réponse anglaise du compositeur Richard Rodgers. Mon ambition était tout aussi folle que la sienne, je voulais devenir une star de la pop, pour toutes les raisons saines que les femmes, l'argent et la célébrité. La différence entre Andrew et moi était que mes rêves n'étaient jamais vitaux pour moi, bien qu'il soit facile de le dire maintenant. Ils auraient pu devenir tels si j'avais échoué. Par conséquent, lorsque Andrew a suggéré une ambition complètement folle pour moi, c'est-à-dire de devenir aussi célèbre qu'Oscar Hammerstein en tant que parolier, je n'ai eu aucun scrupule à essayer. C'était en partie parce que dans dix minutes après notre présentation, il était au piano et m'avait joué trois morceaux qu'il avait composés - je pouvais dire qu'il était bon. Très bon. Au cours des trois morceaux, j'ai été rappelé à l'esprit de nombreux albums de meilleures chansons de mes parents de la collection LP. Il avait besoin d'un nouveau parolier pour le monde extérieur. J'avais peu à lui présenter en retour, à part un instant de louange pour sa musique et un véritable, réellement sorti, disque de sept pouces d'une chanson que j'avais écrite (tous les deux mots et musique) avec laquelle un groupe de pop inconnu avait porté le coup fatal à leur carrière moribonde en l'enregistrant trois mois auparavant. Nous nous sommes quittés, promettant de nous revoir et d'écrire quelque chose ensemble. J'étais toujours plus intéressé par les charts que par le West End Theatre, mais je me suis dit dans le bus qui m'emmenait à mon appartement que j'avais juste rencontré quelqu'un d'une rare capacité et de détermination, et j'aurais été fou de rater l'occasion d'être le compagnon d'un gars qui allait certainement secouer le monde du théâtre musical, probablement la semaine prochaine. Et même si nous n'avons pas réussi à défier les meilleurs compositeurs musicaux avec succès, nous pourrions essayer de renverser les Beatles et les Rolling Stones plus tard, en été. Les Everly Brothers venaient de faire un retour et auraient certainement besoin de nouveaux morceaux. Le lendemain, de retour à mon bureau dans le bureau où je me formais pour devenir avocat, la certitude brève que j'avais connue d'une vie dans le monde du spectacle avec Andrew Lloyd Webber avait quelque peu disparu. Je savais bien sûr que je continuerais à surveiller les petites annonces dans Melody Maker pour des groupes ayant besoin d'un vocaliste, et que je ferais quelques autres chansons de trois accords adaptées non pas pour cacher les limites de ma voix, mais c'était encore des chances de parier que finalement je finirais par traîner à travers mes examens et que je finirais par être un avocat respectable d'ici vingt-cinq ans. D'ici là, je n'aurais certainement plus qu'à regarder les charts de pop et à écrire quelques nouvelles chansons qui imiteraient les paroliers de musiques de comédie plutôt que les pop stars. Et Andrew était un individu fascinant qui parlait de bons guides gastronomiques et d'architecture victorienne, en plus de soutenir le Leyton Orient football team. Je n'étais pas convaincu par l'idée d'un musical qu'il avait été en train de travailler pendant un an, mais en 1965, je n'étais rarement convaincu par quoi que ce soit. Sa talent était indéniable et il prétendait avoir tous les contacts. Je suis rapidement retourné dans son salon. L'idée était la vie du docteur Thomas Barnardo, le philanthrope du dix-neuvième siècle qui a fondé les orphelinats qui portent son nom. Son histoire était digne d'intérêt, mais pas celle qui a vraiment allumé mon imagination. Le héros était trop propre, au moins dans la version d'Andrew de sa vie, et l'entreprise était originale dans la conception et l'exécution, en se basant trop sur le succès de la comédie musicale, Oliver. D'un autre côté, la conviction d'Andrew quant à la précoce brillance de sa partition était contagieuse et pas totalement injustifiée. Qu'est-ce que je savais sur les comédies musicales? Comme David Land, qui plus tard est devenu mon agent pendant un quart de siècle, a dit à plusieurs reprises (et à plusieurs reprises) si il y a une demande pour un hamburger bar sur le bloc, il y a de la place pour deux. Nous pourrions être la deuxième chaîne de hamburgers. J'ai travaillé avec une grande enthousiasme, en particulier pour ces chansons qui devaient être drôles. Andrew a décrit le scénario, m'a joué les airs et, dans de nombreux cas, m'a donné le titre, dont la plupart avaient probablement été pensés par son ancien ami de l'école qui avait déjà essayé. J'ai manqué un jour à la banque d'avocats pour écrire mes premiers lots de paroles de comédies musicales. Je ne savais pas ce jour-là mais j'avais changé de carrière.

results.src_text:
Clutter

Sometimes it seems that no matter how many possessions you have, you never feel secure. While it is reasonable to have a basic nesting instinct and create a home which meets your needs, there is a point where the motivation for acquiring things gets out of control. Modern advertising is moreover deliberately designed to play on our insecurities.If you don’t have one of these you will be a lesser human being is one of the consistent underlying messages we receive. To discover just how much you are influenced, I challenge you to try not to read any advertising billboards next time you go down the street. These multi-million dollar messages relentlessly condition us in very persuasive ways without our ever realising it. We are bombarded by them - television, radio, newspapers, magazines, posters, tee shirts, the internet, you name it - all encouraging us to buy, buy, buy.

Caves

Research establishments and university departments around the world have invested years of research time in all aspects of caves, mainly their origins, their hydrology and their biology. Caves constitute a small but rather mysterious component of the natural environment - as such they arouse our curiosity and challenge our desire for knowledge, and consequently have had a considerable amount of research effort devoted to them. Furthermore, because of their presence as natural phenomena, they have had a long history of study, which has been intensified in those parts of the world where caves have had a direct effect on our way of life. However, the physical agility required to visit many caves means that cave research has been less in the hands of the learned professors than in most other scientific fields. Indeed there is a considerable, perhaps unique, overlap between the professional, scientific study of caves and the amateur studies carried out by those who mainly visit caves for sport.

Weather Watch

Countless observant people without any instruments other than their own senses originally laid the foundations of meteorology, which has progressed since the 17th century into the highly technical science of today. Satellites and electronic instruments relay endless weather information to us with the minimum of delay, computers solve in minutes abstruse mathematical sums at a speed beyond the capability of the human brain. Meteorological theory is peppered with long words which have little meaning to the non-professional. It sometimes seems there is no room left for simple weather wisdom, but nothing could be further from the truth. Rommel

Het lijkt alsof je nooit genoeg bezittingen hebt en toch blijf je je onzeker voelen. Het is natuurlijk verstandig om een basisbehoefte aan een thuis te hebben, maar er is een grens waarbij de motivatie om dingen te kopen uit de hand loopt. De moderne reclame is opzettelijk ontworpen om op onze onzekerheden in te spelen. Als je niet over een van deze bezittingen beschikt, ben je een minderwaardig mens, is een van de onderliggende boodschappen die we steeds weer krijgen. Om te ontdekken hoezeer je beïnvloed wordt, daag ik je uit om de volgende keer dat je de straat opgaat geen reclameborden te lezen. Deze miljoenen dollars aan berichten conditioneren ons op een zeer overtuigende manier zonder dat we het ooit doorhebben. We worden overspoeld door ze - televisie, radio, kranten, tijdschriften, posters, T-shirts, internet, noem maar op - en ze moedigen ons aan om te kopen, te kopen, te kopen.

Grotten

Onderzoekinstellingen en universiteiten over de hele wereld hebben jarenlang onderzoek gedaan naar alle aspecten van grotten, voornamelijk hun oorsprong, hun hydrologie en hun biologie. Grotten vormen een klein maar mysterieus onderdeel van de natuurlijke omgeving - als zodanig wekken ze onze nieuwsgierigheid en drijven ze onze verlangen naar kennis op, waardoor er veel onderzoek naar hen is gedaan. Bovendien hebben ze vanwege hun aanwezigheid als natuurlijk fenomeen een lange geschiedenis van bestudering, die is geïntensiveerd in de delen van de wereld waar grotten een direct effect hebben op ons leven. Echter, vanwege de fysieke behendigheid die vereist is om veel grotten te bezoeken, is het onderzoek naar grotten minder in handen van de geleerden dan in de meeste andere wetenschappelijke velden. Er is een aanzienlijke, misschien unieke, overlapping tussen het professionele, wetenschappelijke onderzoek naar grotten en de amateurstudies die worden uitgevoerd door degenen die grotten vooral bezoeken voor de sport.

results.src_text:
CRYING 

Charles Darwin thought that the human tendency to cry had no obvious evolving purpose. He was almost certainly wrong. More recently scientists have pointed to its social significance, with psychiatrist John Bowlby highlighting the role of crying in developing the attachment between mother and child. Many believe that tears, at least during childhood, are mainly an expression of helplessness. However, the persistence of crying into adulthood is harder to explain. It seems that the sound of crying becomes considerably less important than the visual signal it conveys. It may have been advantageous to early human communities as a means of promoting trust and social connectedness. 
Tears can undoubtedly have other causes too. We may cry to express sympathy for those suffering terrible injustice. Furthermore, tears can be shed involuntarily, rather to our embarrassment, when we hear inspiring music or moving speeches. We may cry when watching a sentimental film, but interestingly, this is more likely to occur in company than when we are alone. The social function of crying would seem to be undeniable, but research continues.

results.title: a114e1e3-6d84-4957-8765-2dfd54467a9b.txt
results.src_text:
We are Talking Big Boots here. Really BIGTIME Boots.
I stood in my 800-dollar-each designer-label cowboy boots on the rocks of an old formation in the Arizona desert sand. Money no object. I wore the whole truly cowboy outfit and if you had the outfit you might be a cowboy. But I was not. It wasn’t working. I squinted info the morning sun looking out at the Arizona mountains and I had to admit, I was not at home on the range,
Flying in from Denver just after dawn, I had the feeling that I just might pass far an ol' cowhand coming in from the sky. The feeling didn’t last past the first real cowboy in the luggage hall of Phoenix airport. He was wearing a sweat-stained I-shirt, needed a shave, and was hoisting a dirty canvas bag off the conveyer belt when he caught sight of my brand new cowboy boots. He slowly raised one eyebrow and moved off out of the door without looking back.
There ought to be, somewhere, hanging in a closet, a suit of clothes an ex-racing driver can put on without feeling like he is from another planet. Something he could wear so that wherever he goes he doesn’t get the feeling that everybody is talking another language and doing whatever they do at half speed. I liked, no, not liked... I flatout loved being a racing driver, driving racing cars. I am addicted to it and it is all I know how to do. But I don’t do it any more. I couldn’t if I wanted to. Question is, I thought, looking into the mean, rust-coloured rock of the mountains in the distance, what do I do now?
A racing driver should have one or two fall-back identities lined up for when he climbs out of his car. I thought I did, but when I reached for them they just disappeared. How about: an ex-racing driver adds colour to the commentary direct from the trackside? 'We got fifteen guys, all of them former Indy and Formula One drivers, fifteen guys in front of you, Forrest, standing in line to be colour commentators. We’ll call you.'
Well then, how about: an ex-racing driver coins a partnership to sell classic cars? That lasted nearly all winter with phone calls, lunches, lawyers und meetings with bankers. But it was the year nobody was buying old Ferraris and Honda was 'reviewing' its dealer list. So in the end I gracefully withdrew before there was nothing to withdraw from. Being an 'ex' anything is depressing work. I mean you tell me, how badly do you want to hear about how I was almost the World Champion? Nobody wants to hear a story that ends in ‘almost'. And even if I had been world champion you could probably just about stand to listen to the story for five minutes before your ears turned to cement. Last year's champion was last year.
Not that I want sympathy. Which is just as well, since I don’t get any. Well, why should I? I had a good run, made money and hung on to enough. But oh, man, I miss the heat of slipping into that graceful, elegant, shrink-wrapped super-tech machine with seven hundred horsepower behind my neck. Zero to a hundred and fifty miles an hour in 4,9 seconds. And yes, I miss coming within an eyelash of killing myself every race or so. I miss the bright and gorgeous people and the reporters who acted as if what I said mattered. Being famous, even in a minor way, isn't all bad. Businessmen and politicians bragged to their friends that they knew me. Little boys slid under fences to get my autograph. And now that I don’t drive a racing car... Only last week the phone rang twice. I have time in the morning and I have time in the afternoon. And let me just check, but I think tomorrow is free, so much empty time.
I looked up into the soft blue morning sky. No buzzards overhead. Maybe Arizona doesn't have buzzards. But a couple of little brown birds in a saguaro cactus just in front of me were giving me advice, something like 'get away from our nest before we sing our hearts out’. It had never occurred to me that the desert had songbirds. It did occur to me that a bogus cowboy in designer boots had a lot to learn.

J'avais tout l'habit de cow-boy vraiment et si vous aviez l'habit, vous pourriez être un cow-boy. Mais je ne l'étais pas. Cela ne marchait pas. Je plissais les yeux sous le soleil du matin en regardant les montagnes de l'Arizona et je devais admettre que je ne me sentais pas à la maison sur la piste. En descendant de l'avion à Phoenix, je me suis senti comme si j'allais peut-être croiser un cow-boy en arrivant du ciel. Ce sentiment n'a pas duré après avoir vu le premier vrai cow-boy dans le hall des bagages. Il portait un t-shirt trempé de sueur, avait besoin d'un rasage et soulevait lentement une mèche de sourcil en sortant de la porte sans se retourner. Il devait y avoir, quelque part, dans un placard, une tenue d'un ancien pilote de course qu'il pourrait mettre sans se sentir comme s'il venait d'une autre planète. Quelque chose qu'il pourrait porter de sorte que partout où il irait, il n'aurait pas l'impression que tout le monde parle une langue différente et fait ce qu'ils font à moitié-vitesse. J'aimais, non, j'adorais être un pilote de course, conduire des voitures de course. Je suis accro et c'est tout ce que je sais faire. Mais je ne le fais plus. Je ne pourrais pas si je le voulais. La question est, je me suis demandé en regardant les rochers roux et rougeâtres des montagnes au loin, que faire maintenant? Un pilote de course devrait avoir une ou deux identités de rechange en attente quand il descend de sa voiture. J'avais cru que j'en avais, mais quand je me suis mis à les chercher, elles ont simplement disparu. Comment faire? Un ancien pilote de course ajoute de la couleur aux commentaires directs depuis la piste? 'Nous avons quinze gars, tous anciens pilotes de Formule Un et Indy, quinze gars devant vous, Forrest, en ligne pour être commentateurs. Nous vous appellerons.' Eh bien, alors, comment faire? Un ancien pilote de course crée une société de vente de voitures de collection? Cela a duré presque tout l'hiver avec des appels téléphoniques, des déjeuners, des avocats et des réunions avec des banquiers. Mais c'était l'année où personne ne voulait acheter de vieilles Ferrari et Honda 'révisait' sa liste de concessionnaires. Donc, en fin de compte, j'ai retiré avec élégance avant qu'il n'y ait rien à retirer. Être un 'ancien' de quelque chose est un travail déprimant. Je veux dire, dites-moi, à quel point voulez-vous entendre parler de comment j'ai failli être champion du monde? Personne ne veut entendre une histoire qui se termine par 'presque'. Et même si j'avais été champion du monde, vous pouvez probablement écouter l'histoire pendant cinq minutes avant que vos oreilles ne deviennent du ciment. Le champion de l'année dernière était l'année dernière. Pas que je veuille de la sympathie. C'est bien que ça soit ainsi, car je n'en reçois pas. Eh bien, pourquoi devrais-je en recevoir? J'ai eu une bonne carrière, j'ai gagné de l'argent et j'en ai conservé assez. Mais, oh, homme, j'ai envie de me glisser dans cette machine élégante et enveloppante, dotée de 700 chevaux derrière mon cou. De zéro à 150 miles à l'heure en 4,9 secondes. Et oui, j'ai envie de me retrouver à peine au-dessus de la mort à chaque course ou presque. J'ai envie des gens brillants et superbes et des journalistes qui agissent comme si ce que je dis importait. Être célèbre, même dans une mesure mineure, n'est pas si mal. Les hommes d'affaires et les hommes politiques se vantent à leurs amis du fait qu'ils me connaissent. Les petits garçons glissent sous les clôtures pour obtenir mon autographe. Et maintenant que je ne conduis pas une voiture de course... Récemment, le téléphone a sonné deux fois. J'ai du temps le matin et j'ai du temps l'après-midi. Et laissez-moi juste vérifier, mais je crois que demain est libre, beaucoup de temps vide. J'ai regardé dans le ciel bleu matinal doux. Aucun buse au-dessus. Peut-être que l'Arizona n'a pas de buses. Mais deux petits oiseaux bruns dans un cactus de saguaro juste devant moi me donnaient des conseils, quelque chose comme'sors de notre nid avant que nous ne chantions de tout cœur'. Il ne m'était jamais venu à l'idée que le désert avait des oiseaux chanteurs. Il m'est venu à l'idée que le cow-boy en bottes de design avait beaucoup à apprendre.
results.back_text: I was wearing my $800 cowboy boots on the rocks of an ancient Arizona desert sand formation. Money was no object. I had the whole cowboy outfit really and if you had the outfit, you could be a cowboy. But I wasn't. It didn't work. I squinted my eyes under the morning sun looking at the Arizona mountains and had to admit that I didn't feel at home on the track. As I got off the plane in Phoenix, I felt as if I might bump into a cowboy coming down from the sky. That feeling didn't last after seeing the first real cowboy in the baggage claim hall. He was wearing a sweat-soaked t-shirt, needed a shave and was slowly lifting a eyebrow as he walked out the door without turning around. There must be, somewhere, in a closet, a suit of an old race car driver that he could put on without feeling like he was from another planet. Something he could wear so that wherever he went, he wouldn't feel like everyone was speaking a different language and doing what they do at half-speed. I loved, no, I adored being a race car driver, driving race cars. I'm hooked and that's all I know how to do. But I don't do it anymore. I couldn't if I wanted to. The question is, I wondered as I looked at the red and reddish-brown rocks of the mountains in the distance, what now? A race car driver should have one or two backup identities waiting when he steps out of his car. I thought I had, but when I started looking for them, they just disappeared. What to do? An old race car driver adds color to the direct commentary from the track? 'We have fifteen guys, all former Formula One and Indy race car drivers, fifteen guys in front of you, Forrest, on line to be commentators. We'll call you.' Well, then, what to do? An old race car driver creates a collector car sales company? It lasted almost all winter with phone calls, lunches, lawyers and meetings with bankers. But it was the year when nobody wanted to buy old Ferraris and Honda was'revising' its list of dealers. So, in the end, I gracefully withdrew before there was nothing to withdraw from. Being an 'ex' of something is a depressing job. I mean, tell me, how much do you want to hear about how I almost became world champion? Nobody wants to hear a story that ends with 'almost'. And even if I had become world champion, you can probably listen to the story for five minutes before your ears become cement. The champion of the previous year was the previous year. Not that I want sympathy. It's fine that it's like that, because I don't get any. Well, why should I? I had a good career, I made money and I saved enough. But, oh, man, I want to slip into that elegant, enveloping machine with 700 horses behind my neck. From zero to 150 miles per hour in 4.9 seconds. And yes, I want to find myself barely above death at every race or almost. I want brilliant and beautiful people and journalists who act as if what I say matters. Being famous, even to a minor extent, is not so bad. Businessmen and politicians brag to their friends about knowing me. Little boys slide under the fences to get my autograph. And now that I'm not driving a race car... Recently, the phone rang twice. I have time in the morning and time in the afternoon. And let me just check, but I think tomorrow is free, a lot of empty time. I looked at the soft, gentle morning sky. No buzzards above. Maybe Arizona doesn't have buzzards. But two little brown birds in a saguaro cactus just in front of me were giving me advice, something like 'get out of our nest before we sing our hearts out'. It never occurred to me that the desert had singing birds. It occurred to me that the cowboy in the $800 design boots had a lot to learn.

results.src_text:
Running a business in the countryside 

Five women talk about their experiences setting up a business in the countryside. 

A.
‘My customers are friends,' says CHRISTINE HOGAN, who runs a computer-aided design business with a turnover of over £200,000 a year and four full-time employees. 'My husband and I moved out of London to the country when our children were small, and I wanted work I could do at home. I had worked with computers before I was married, so my husband suggested I set up a computer-aided design business. It needed a huge amount of money and things were difficult in the beginning. But I have been very careful, making sure that I told the bank manager if I was likely to overspend. Being in the house is a big saving, and I can carry on working in the evening if I want. It has remained a small business. We hardly ever deliver work - people from the area tend to collect it from us.' 

B.
’I enjoy being independent,' says MAGGY SASANOW, who works from home as a designer of greetings cards. 'I trained in art at university, and wanted to work in a museum. But when I married, we went to live in the countryside, where there wasn't that sort of work. So I decided to set up my own business and I produce a range of 50 greetings cards which I sell to museums. I work in a big room upstairs. The disadvantage of working from home is that there is always something that needs doing - like mowing the lawn. My business comes completely by word of mouth - I don't advertise at all. People send work down from London as I am cheaper than other artists. Working alone, I don't get to exchange ideas with other people any more, but generally there are more advantages than disadvantages.' 

C.
’It has been hard at times,' says DELIA TURNER, whose curtain-making business has seen good times and bad. 'I started my business eight years ago. Then this type of business was expanding, and in two years my turnover went from £24,000 to £80,000. I used to manage six full-time curtain-makers. But I had to sack them because of the decline in the economy, which was painful because it is not easy to find other jobs in this area. I am right back almost to where I started, making the curtains at home myself, with my husband's help, and using women who work from their homes. I have to be prepared to cut my prices when it's necessary and to look at different opportunities.' 

D.
TESSA STRICKLAND runs the editorial and production side of her children's book publishing business from her farmhouse. 'I moved to the countryside three years ago for two reasons. The first was financial, because London was so expensive, and the second was because I love the country. I enjoy being able to work when I want to. Eighty per cent of my income comes from deals with Australia, the Far East and North America, so I have to take calls at odd hours. The disadvantage is that it requires discipline to shut the office door. I publish children's books from cultures around the world, working with authors and artists. All my professional experience had been in London, so I used to feel very alone at first.' 

E.
MEG RIVERS runs a cakes-by-post business and a shop with a turnover of £250,000 a year and employs six people, some part-time. 'I started ten years ago at home. I am very interested in health, so I started making fruit cakes, using good quality flour and eggs. Then I started getting requests from friends and relatives, and soon I was sending cakes all over the country. Seven years ago I rented a small building and everything is made there - we have a baker and assistant, and a professional cake-icer. I don't cook at all now, as I run the commercial side. My greatest problem has been the financial side of the business, which has been difficult simply because we didn't have an enormous amount of money to set up with.'
results.tgt_text: Vijf vrouwen vertellen over hun ervaringen met het opzetten van een bedrijf in het platteland. A. ‘Mijn klanten zijn vrienden,’ zegt CHRISTINE HOGAN, die een bedrijf voor computerondersteunde ontwerpen runt met een omzet van meer dan £200.000 per jaar en vier voltijdse werknemers. ‘Mijn man en ik zijn naar het platteland verhuisd toen onze kinderen klein waren en ik wilde een baan die ik thuis kon doen. Ik had al met computers gewerkt voordat ik getrouwd was, dus mijn man stelde voor dat ik een bedrijf voor computerondersteunde ontwerpen zou opzetten. Dat vereiste een enorme hoeveelheid geld en het was moeilijk in het begin. Maar ik ben heel voorzichtig geweest en heb ervoor gezorgd dat ik de bankdirecteur op de hoogte hield als ik de kans zag dat ik te veel geld zou uitgeven. Het feit dat ik in huis werk is een groot voordeel, en ik kan's avonds doorwerken als ik dat wil. Het is gebleven een klein bedrijf. We leveren bijna nooit werk af - mensen uit de regio halen het meestal bij ons op.’ B. ‘Ik geniet van de onafhankelijkheid,’ zegt MAGGY SASANOW, die vanuit huis werkt als ontwerpster van wenskaarten. ‘Ik heb kunst gestudeerd aan de universiteit en wilde graag in een museum werken. Maar toen we met mijn man naar het platteland verhuisden, was er daar niet zoiets. Dus ik besloot een eigen bedrijf op te zetten en produceer een reeks van 50 wenskaarten die ik aan musea verkoop. Ik werk in een grote kamer bovenin het huis. Het nadeel van thuiswerken is dat er altijd iets is dat gedaan moet worden - zoals het gazon maaien. Mijn bedrijf komt volledig door mond-tot-mondreclame. Ik adverteer helemaal niet. Mensen sturen werk vanuit Londen naar me toe omdat ik goedkoper ben dan andere kunstenaars. Door alleen te werken, kom ik niet meer in contact met andere mensen, maar over het algemeen zijn er meer voordelen dan nadelen.’ C. ‘Het is soms moeilijk geweest,’ zegt DELIA TURNER, wiens gordijnenmakerij goede en slechte tijden heeft gekend. ‘Ik begon mijn bedrijf acht jaar geleden. Toen was dit type bedrijf in opkomst en binnen twee jaar steeg mijn omzet van £24.000 naar £80.000. Ik had toen zes voltijdse gordijnenmakers in dienst. Maar ik moest ze ontslaan vanwege de economische crisis, wat pijnlijk was omdat het niet makkelijk is om andere banen in deze regio te vinden. Ik ben bijna terug bij het begin, waarbij ik de gordijnen zelf thuis maak, met de hulp van mijn man, en ik gebruik thuiswerkers. Ik moet bereid zijn om mijn prijzen te verlagen als dat nodig is en op zoek naar andere mogelijkheden.’ D. TESSA STRICKLAND beheert de redactie- en productiekant van haar kinderboekenuitgeverij vanuit haar boerderij. ‘Ik verhuisde drie jaar geleden naar het platteland om twee redenen. De eerste was financiële, omdat Londen zo duur was, en de tweede was omdat ik van het platteland houd. Ik geniet ervan om te kunnen werken wanneer ik wil. Achtendertig procent van mijn inkomen komt van deals met Australië, het Verre Oosten en Noord-Amerika, dus ik moet op vreemde tijden bellen. Het nadeel is dat het discipline vereist om de deur van het kantoor te sluiten. Ik publiceer kinderboeken uit culturen over de hele wereld, samenwerking met auteurs en kunstenaars. Al mijn professionele ervaring was in Londen, dus ik voelde me eerst erg alleen.’ E. MEEG RIVERS runt een bedrijf voor cakes per post en een winkel met een omzet van £250.000 per jaar en heeft zes werknemers, waarvan sommigen deeltijds. ‘Ik begon tien jaar geleden thuis. Ik ben erg geïnteresseerd in gezondheid, dus ik begon met het maken van fruitcake, met goede kwaliteit meel en eieren. Toen kreeg ik verzoeken van vrienden en familieleden en al snel stuurde ik cakes over het hele land. Zeven jaar geleden huurde ik een klein pand en alles wordt daar gemaakt - we hebben een bakker en assistent en een professionele cake-icer. Ik kook helemaal niet meer nu, omdat ik de commerciële kant beheer. Mijn grootste probleem was het financiële aspect van het bedrijf, wat moeilijk was omdat we niet veel geld hadden om te beginnen.’
